tool_schemas.description: Release history for a service with health status (oldest first).

tool_schemas.name: rollback
tool_schemas.description: Roll a service back to a previously released version in all production regions.

tool_schemas.description: Deploy a version of a service to all production regions.

tool_schemas.name: create_incident
tool_schemas.description: Open an incident; this pages the on-call engineer.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. Requests repeated with the same key are executed at most once.

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the checkout-api v2.3.1 deploy to production, the service failed health checks in all regions, with an error rate of 18%. I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in us-east, us-west and eu-west. v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so I didn't use it. After the rollback, the service is healthy in all regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next step: find out what in v2.3.1 caused the failures before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback target:** v2.3.0 is the newest release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so I didn't use it.
- **Rollback:** Before the rollback, v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west and failing health checks, with an 18% error rate. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 for checkout-api. It records the failed v2.3.1 deploy, the rollback to v2.3.0, why that version was chosen and the recovery. It also says v2.3.1 shouldn't be redeployed until someone finds out what caused the failures.

content.text: Most recent production-healthy release is v2.3.0 (v2.3.1-rc was only healthy in staging, so it doesn't qualify).
